name: Should I choose 2x4 or 2x6 studs for my garage walls?

mainEntity.name: Should I choose 2x4 or 2x6 studs for my garage walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choosing 2x4 framing is sufficient for basic utility walls, room dividers, and unconditioned storage where floor space is at a premium. However, choosing 2x6 framing gives you deeper wall cavities that accommodate R-19 or R-21 insulation, making it the better choice if you plan to heat or cool the garage year-round. While 2x6 framing costs slightly more in materials and reduces the interior floor footprint by two inches per side, it provides significantly better thermal performance and a sturdier structure for mounting heavy wall cabinets.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use 2x4s for standard division and saving floor space; choose 2x6s if you intend to insulate, heat, or cool the garage, or need heavier load capacity for storage.
